Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  

  

Under the close supervision of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientists will participate in the less complex scientific, analytical, and technical work to support the Department of Pesticide Regulation’s (DPR) Pesticide Use Reporting (PUR) Program. These positions support DPR’s mission to protect public health and the environment by improving the accuracy, accessibility, and understanding of pesticide use data statewide. Site visits may also occur in urban and suburban environments. Site visits will occur under various climatic conditions that may require exposure to high heat, full sun, high humidity, wind, and rain.

Under direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (EPM I) (Supervisory), the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) performs a range of duties involving supervision of staff, data analysis, research projects and stakeholder engagement for the Citrus Division. This involves interaction with federal, State, and county agencies as well as other cooperators and interested or affected groups.  

The Citrus Pest and Disease Prevention Division's headquarters is conveniently located in South Natomas. The location offers free parking and is within walking distance of retail centers containing restaurants.

The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.  

The primary responsibilities of the Citrus Pest and Disease Prevention Division (Citrus Division) are detection, suppression, and eradication of Asian citrus psyllid (ACP) and Huanglongbing (HLB) throughout the State. Due to the expansions of ACP and HLB, it is imperative that ACP control and HLB eradication activities be enhanced and quarantine regulation enforcement measured. The Citrus Division will carry out HLB eradication and ACP control in a systematic and consistent manner that addresses local conditions, while augmenting quarantine regulation enforcement activities in existing and newly detected areas. These activities are accomplished through the operation of a statewide detection trapping program, ACP and HLB surveys, emergency treatment and response, and implementation of environmental monitoring practices. This is provided through general, federal, and industry\-funded programs. The Citrus Division consults with the Primary State Scientists, global subject matter experts (Technical Working Groups), and regulatory agencies (Department of Pesticide Regulation, Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment, and the California Environmental Protection Agency. The Citrus Division will operate out of field offices located within three geographical districts. Each district works under the general direction of the Sacramento headquarters staff and the director of the Citrus Division.

The California Coastal Commission is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist or Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join its Ecology Team (Technical Services Unit) at its Headquarters Office in downtown San Francisco. This position will primarily focus on the relationship between wildfire and coastal ecology as relates to vegetation management for fuel reduction, ecological restoration, and resilience work across a range of ecosystems, including forests, shrublands, grasslands and wetlands throughout the coastal zone, which extends inland from the shoreline at variable distances up to more than five miles in some areas.


The Commission is a small State agency that is charged with protecting coastal resources and managing coastal development in California. The Commission’s mission is to implement the Coastal Act and to protect, restore, and enhance coastal and marine resources for the continuing benefit of current and future generations. It carries out this mandate through regulatory and planning actions related to development within offshore waters and on land along the California coast. The Commission also has authority under the federal Coastal Zone Management Act to review federal and federally\-permitted activities such as dredging, military training exercises, wildland management, and highway projects that affect resources of the coastal zone.


The Ecology Team generally supports the Commission and its staff with technical review and analysis of potential effects on the coast’s sensitive natural resources associated with proposed development projects. Duties will be adjusted commensurately to the level at which the position is filled. Generally, the incumbent will be expected to: review and analyze a variety of technical reports including CEQA/NEPA documents, technical surveys and memoranda, restoration and mitigation plans, and scientific literature; conduct research and investigations often involving complex environmental conditions and circumstances; identify problems including potential adverse impacts to coastal resources and means to avoid and minimize these; factor in climate change dynamics relative to environmental considerations; coordinate with other federal, state, and local agencies; and, make recommendations for conformance with the natural resource policies of the Coastal Act and relevant certified plans.

The incumbent may also represent the Commission staff on multi\-agency work groups, task forces, and similar entities; and coordinate with staff of local, state, and federal agencies; the legislature; stakeholder groups; and the broader public.


The position offers considerable opportunity for developing and contributing expertise on a range of ecosystems as well as relevant and emerging issues related to coastal ecology and wildfire resilience in California’s coastal landscape.

The California Coastal Commission is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist or Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join its Ecology Team (Technical Services Unit) at its Headquarters Office in downtown San Francisco. The Commission is a small State agency that is charged with protecting coastal resources and managing coastal development in California. Duties will be adjusted commensurately to the level at which the position is filled. The incumbent may also represent the Commission staff on multi\-agency work groups, task forces, and similar entities; and coordinate with staff of local, state, and federal agencies; the legislature; stakeholder groups; and the broader public.
